standing_assumptions:
The work is a three-page comment (Statistical Science 32(3), 2017, pp. 346–348; PDF pp. 1–3) on Ding (2017), ‘A paradox from randomization-based causal inference’. It has no numbered theorem, proposition, lemma or equation, and no proof, table, figure or appendix; its mathematics is in unnumbered displays and sentences of Sections 2–4. All three page images were read, and everything quoted below was transcribed from them.

(S1) Scope. Introduction, p. 346 (PDF p. 1): ‘Note, we consider only asymptotic results, and do not discuss the finite $N$ differences between exact tests and tests that are only known to be asymptotically valid. Finite $N$ differences may account in part for Ding’s (2017) simulation results; while perhaps of practical importance, such differences are in our view theoretically uninteresting as the source of a potential paradox.’

(S2) Design and regularity conditions. Section 2, p. 347 (PDF p. 2), in brackets: ‘[We follow Ding’s, 2017 notation throughout. We will also assume complete random assignment with the asymptotic scaling and regularity conditions of Freedman, 2008, primarily bounded fourth (cross) moments on the limit distribution of potential outcomes with $\lim_{N\to\infty}N_1/N=p$, where $0<p<1$. These regularity conditions appear to be acknowledged in the final paragraph of Ding, 2017.]’

(S3) Notation that the comment prints. p. 346 (PDF p. 1): ‘Fisher’s randomization test (FRT)’; ‘the FRT (with the difference in means as a test statistic)’; ‘the null of zero average causal effect (Neyman’s null)’; ‘the sharp null of zero individual causal effects (Fisher’s null)’; the Wald-type analogue is ‘a Wald test assuming a homoskedastic linear model’ and is ‘equivalent to a pooled-variance two-sample $z$-test’. p. 347 (PDF p. 2): ‘the null hypothesis, $\tau=\overline{Y}_1-\overline{Y}_0=0$’; ‘using as a working assumption $\tau=\widehat{\tau}$’; ‘the variance of the FRT reference distribution, $\widehat{V}(\text{Fisher})$’; ‘the variance estimator associated with the Wald-type analogue’, referred to as $\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})$; ‘one of Neyman’s variance estimators, $\widehat{V}(\text{Neyman})$’; $V(\widehat{\tau})$; ‘where $p=\lim_{N\to\infty}N_1/N$’. p. 348 (PDF p. 3): ‘Fisher’s null can be viewed as a joint hypothesis that implies two features of the underlying distribution of potential outcomes: $\tau=0$ and $S_1=S_0$. Neyman’s null implies no such assumption about $S_1=S_0$.’ The comment prints no definition of $N_1$, $N_0$, $S_1$, $S_0$, $\widehat{\tau}$, $V(\widehat{\tau})$ or of the three variance estimators: it takes them from Ding (2017), which is not staged.

(S4) The audit's reading of that notation (used by both fresh readers and by the validators; not printed in the comment). For each $N$ there is a finite population of units $i=1,\ldots,N$ with fixed real potential outcomes $Y_i(1)$ and $Y_i(0)$. $\overline{Y}_1=N^{-1}\sum_iY_i(1)$, $\overline{Y}_0=N^{-1}\sum_iY_i(0)$, $\tau_i=Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)$, $\tau=\overline{Y}_1-\overline{Y}_0$. $S_1^2=(N-1)^{-1}\sum_i(Y_i(1)-\overline{Y}_1)^2$, $S_0^2=(N-1)^{-1}\sum_i(Y_i(0)-\overline{Y}_0)^2$, $S_\tau^2=(N-1)^{-1}\sum_i(\tau_i-\tau)^2$; $S_1\ge0$ and $S_0\ge0$ are the square roots. Complete random assignment: $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_N)$ is uniformly distributed on $\Omega_N=\{z\in\{0,1\}^N:\sum_iz_i=N_1\}$, with $N_0=N-N_1$; this is the only randomness, and $E$, $V$ and probabilities refer to it. Observed outcome $Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Z_iY_i(1)+(1-Z_i)Y_i(0)$. Arm means $\overline{Y}_1^{\mathrm{obs}}=N_1^{-1}\sum_iZ_iY_i^{\mathrm{obs}}$ and $\overline{Y}_0^{\mathrm{obs}}=N_0^{-1}\sum_i(1-Z_i)Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}$; the difference in means is $\widehat{\tau}=\overline{Y}_1^{\mathrm{obs}}-\overline{Y}_0^{\mathrm{obs}}$, and $V(\widehat{\tau})$ is its variance. Arm sample variances $s_1^2=(N_1-1)^{-1}\sum_iZ_i(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\overline{Y}_1^{\mathrm{obs}})^2$ and $s_0^2=(N_0-1)^{-1}\sum_i(1-Z_i)(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\overline{Y}_0^{\mathrm{obs}})^2$ (so $N_1\ge2$ and $N_0\ge2$ wherever they appear). $\widehat{V}(\text{Neyman})=s_1^2/N_1+s_0^2/N_0$. $SSR=(N_1-1)s_1^2+(N_0-1)s_0^2$ is the residual sum of squares of the least-squares regression of $Y^{\mathrm{obs}}$ on an intercept and $Z$, whose coefficient on $Z$ is $\widehat{\tau}$; $\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})=\frac{SSR}{N-2}\left(\frac{1}{N_1}+\frac{1}{N_0}\right)=\frac{N\,SSR}{N_1N_0(N-2)}$ is the classical homoskedastic variance estimate of that coefficient (the pooled-variance two-sample form). $s^2=(N-1)^{-1}\sum_i(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\overline{Y}^{\mathrm{obs}})^2$, with $\overline{Y}^{\mathrm{obs}}=N^{-1}\sum_iY_i^{\mathrm{obs}}$, is the variance of the combined observed sample. The FRT reference distribution is the distribution of $D(Z')=N_1^{-1}\sum_iZ'_iY_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-N_0^{-1}\sum_i(1-Z'_i)Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}$ when the observed outcomes are held fixed and $Z'$ is uniform on $\Omega_N$; $\widehat{V}(\text{Fisher})$ is its variance, which equals $\frac{N\,s^2}{N_1N_0}$. Fisher's null: $Y_i(1)=Y_i(0)$ for every $i$. Neyman's null: $\tau=0$. Constant effects: $Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)=\tau$ for every $i$. The divisors ($N-1$ in $S_1^2$, $S_0^2$, $S_\tau^2$ and $s^2$; $N-2$ in $\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})$) are the fresh readers' conventions: the exact finite lemmas listed with the targets depend on them, the asymptotic statements do not.

(S5) The audit's reading of the asymptotic statements (the comment prints only S2). A sequence of finite populations indexed by $N\to\infty$, the potential outcomes and $N_1$ depending on $N$, with $N_1/N\to p$ and $0<p<1$; $S_1^2\to\sigma_1^2$, $S_0^2\to\sigma_0^2$, $S_\tau^2\to\sigma_\tau^2$ and $\tau=\tau_N\to\tau_\infty$, all finite; and $\sup_NN^{-1}\sum_i\left(Y_i(1)^4+Y_i(0)^4\right)<\infty$. For random variables $X_N$ defined on the randomization distributions, $X_N=o_p(N^{-1})$ means that $NX_N\to0$ in probability, and $\operatorname{plim}$ is the limit in probability. In its limit statements the comment writes $S_1$, $S_0$ for the limits $\sigma_1$, $\sigma_0$ (for example ‘$\lim_{N\to\infty}NV(\widehat{\tau})\le S_1^2/p+S_0^2/(1-p)$’, p. 347). Freedman (2008) and Ding (2017) are not staged, so the exact form of their conditions was not checked against the originals.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Section 2, unnumbered statements on the Wald-type analogue: a Wald-type test using $\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})$ is an asymptotically valid test of Fisher's null, and $\widehat{V}(\text{Fisher})-\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})=o_p(N^{-1})$ under local alternatives $\tau_N=o(1)$; Introduction, item (i)
canonical_claim.location: p. 347 (PDF p. 2), Section 2, foot of the left column and right column; Introduction, item (i), p. 346 (PDF p. 1); the sentence on the randomization basis of the Wald variance is in Section 2, p. 346 (PDF p. 1), right column
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: [Wald-type analogue; $\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})$] p. 346, Section 2: ‘Freedman (2008) considers the operating characteristics of a Wald test assuming a homoskedastic linear model; Samii and Aronow (2012) give the implied variance of this test a randomization basis, by establishing that the implied variance is equivalent to the randomization distribution of the difference-in-means estimator if the treatment effect is assumed to be constant and equal to the observed estimate.’ p. 347: ‘The Wald test statistic, however, is constructed in part from the empirical distribution, using as a working assumption $\tau=\widehat{\tau}$ in order to construct a reference distribution local to the observed data.’ S4: $\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})=\frac{SSR}{N-2}\left(\frac1{N_1}+\frac1{N_0}\right)$; the Wald-type test compares $\widehat{\tau}/\sqrt{\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})}$ with standard normal quantiles (not printed). [$\widehat{V}(\text{Fisher})$, $V(\widehat{\tau})$, $\widehat{\tau}$, $\tau$] S3, S4, as in P053-T5. [Fisher's null; Neyman's null; constant effects] p. 346 and S4. [Pitman-type local alternatives of the form $\tau_N=o(1)$] the average effect of the $N$th population tends to zero; this class is wider than the usual $N^{-1/2}$ neighbourhood, and the statement holds for it (Opus reader). [Asymptotically valid test] Not defined; read as: rejection probability under the null tending to the nominal level. [$o_p(N^{-1})$; standing conditions] S5.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: (L4) [Exact difference] $\widehat{V}(\text{Fisher})=\frac{N\,SSR}{N_1N_0(N-1)}+\frac{\widehat{\tau}^2}{N-1}$ and $\widehat{V}(\text{Fisher})-\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})=\frac{\widehat{\tau}^2}{N-1}-\frac{N\,SSR}{N_1N_0(N-1)(N-2)}=\frac{\widehat{\tau}^2-\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})}{N-1}$, for every $z\in\Omega_N$. (L5) [Randomization mean and variance of the difference in means] $E[\widehat{\tau}]=\tau$ and $V(\widehat{\tau})=\frac{S_1^2}{N_1}+\frac{S_0^2}{N_0}-\frac{S_\tau^2}{N}$. (L7) [Constant effects] If $Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)=\tau$ for every $i$, then $S_1^2=S_0^2=:S^2$, $S_\tau^2=0$ and $V(\widehat{\tau})=S^2\left(\frac{1}{N_1}+\frac{1}{N_0}\right)=\frac{N\,S^2}{N_1N_0}$; moreover $E[SSR]=(N-2)S^2$, so that $E[\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})]=V(\widehat{\tau})$. (L8) [Randomization basis of $\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})$; the corrected form of the sentence of p. 346 discussed in the note] Fix $z\in\Omega_N$ and the observed outcomes $y_i$, put $t=\widehat{\tau}(z)$ and $r_i=y_i-t\,z_i$ (the control outcomes imputed under a constant effect equal to the observed estimate). For $Z'$ uniform on $\Omega_N$, the difference in means of the imputed outcomes $r_i+t\,Z'_i$, namely $T(Z')=t+N_1^{-1}\sum_iZ'_ir_i-N_0^{-1}\sum_i(1-Z'_i)r_i$, has mean $t$ and variance $\frac{N\,SSR}{N_1N_0(N-1)}=\frac{N-2}{N-1}\,\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})$. (L1) [Decomposition of the combined variance] For every $z\in\Omega_N$ and all real observed outcomes: $(N-1)s^2=SSR+\frac{N_1N_0}{N}\widehat{\tau}^2$, with $SSR=(N_1-1)s_1^2+(N_0-1)s_0^2$. (L2) [Variance of the FRT reference distribution] For fixed real $y_1,\ldots,y_N$ and $Z'$ uniform on $\Omega_N$, $D(Z')=N_1^{-1}\sum_iZ'_iy_i-N_0^{-1}\sum_i(1-Z'_i)y_i$ has mean $0$ and variance $\frac{N}{N_1N_0}\cdot\frac{1}{N-1}\sum_i(y_i-\bar{y})^2$; hence $\widehat{V}(\text{Fisher})=\frac{N\,s^2}{N_1N_0}$. Provenance. None of these is printed in the comment, which gives no derivations. (L1)–(L5) are the fresh readers' exact identities (fresh-opus/notes.md, ‘Section 2 displays’ and ‘Section 3’; fresh-sol/notes.md, ‘Derivation checks completed’, items 1 and 4; candidates.json, held_up), confirmed by them by complete enumeration in exact arithmetic ($N=8$, $N_1=3$; $N=5$, $N_1=2$). The first sentence of (L7) is the readers' (candidates.json, held_up: ‘the pooled Wald test is valid under the sharp null and under constant effects’); the expectation $E[SSR]=(N-2)S^2$ is not in the comment or in the readers' records: it follows from (L1) and (L2) applied to the fixed vector $Y_i(0)$, of which $SSR$ is the residual sum of squares under constant effects, and it was checked by complete enumeration in exact arithmetic when this list was fixed. (L8) is the batch validator's derivation for P053-N001 (the artifact named below; exact enumeration of the 56 assignments for $N=8$, $N_1=3$: variance $3344/1575$, $\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})=1672/675$, ratio $6/7$), also found by the Opus reader. How the limits follow: (a) from (L4), since $\widehat{\tau}\to0$ and $\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})\to0$ in probability; (b) from (L7) and the consistency of $SSR/(N-2)$ for $S^2$, with (L4) for the Fisher form; (c) from (b) and the finite-population central limit theorem for $\widehat{\tau}/\sqrt{V(\widehat{\tau})}$.
canonical_claim.note: The sentence of p. 346 quoted under the definitions is the subject of clarity note P053-N001: it sets a variance ‘equivalent to’ a distribution, and the words ‘the variance of’ are missing before ‘the randomization distribution’. With them restored (Sol's smallest repair: ‘equivalent to the variance of the randomization distribution’) its exact content is lemma (L8): the two differ by the factor $(N-2)/(N-1)$, so the equivalence is asymptotic, within the comment's stated scope (S1). It is a clarity note, not an error, and has no corrected-statement target of its own; (L8) is its formal content. Samii and Aronow (2012) and Freedman (2008) are not staged, so the attributions were not checked against the originals. The Introduction sentence ‘a Wald-type analogue ... exists (...) is a valid test’ is transcribed as printed (two predicates).

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Section 3, unnumbered statements: Neyman's bound $\lim_{N\to\infty}NV(\widehat{\tau})\le S_1^2/p+S_0^2/(1-p)$, equality under constant effects, agreement of $\widehat{V}(\text{Neyman})$ and $\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})$ under constant effects, and the existence of limit distributions for which $\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})$ is anticonservative
canonical_claim.location: p. 347 (PDF p. 2), Section 3, foot of the right column, continuing at the top of the left column of p. 348 (PDF p. 3)
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: [$V(\widehat{\tau})$] Not defined in the comment; S4: the variance of the difference in means over complete randomization. [$S_1$, $S_0$ inside the limits] the limits $\sigma_1$, $\sigma_0$ (S5); $S_\tau^2$ (S4) is the finite-population variance of the unit effects $\tau_i$, with limit $\sigma_\tau^2$; it is not printed in the comment and enters through Neyman's variance formula (lemma L5). [$p$] printed, p. 347: ‘where $p=\lim_{N\to\infty}N_1/N$’. [Constant effects] S4: $Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)$ the same for every $i$. [$\widehat{V}(\text{Neyman})$, $\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})$] S4, as in P053-T7. [Asymptotically agree] read as $N[\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})-\widehat{V}(\text{Neyman})]\to0$ in probability. [Limit distributions] the limiting second moments $(\sigma_1^2,\sigma_0^2,\sigma_\tau^2)$ and $p$ of a sequence satisfying S5. [Neyman's null] $\tau=0$ (p. 346).
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: (L5) [Randomization mean and variance of the difference in means] $E[\widehat{\tau}]=\tau$ and $V(\widehat{\tau})=\frac{S_1^2}{N_1}+\frac{S_0^2}{N_0}-\frac{S_\tau^2}{N}$. (L6) [Arm sample variances] $E[s_1^2]=S_1^2$ and $E[s_0^2]=S_0^2$; hence $E[\widehat{V}(\text{Neyman})]=\frac{S_1^2}{N_1}+\frac{S_0^2}{N_0}\ge V(\widehat{\tau})$. (L7) [Constant effects] If $Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)=\tau$ for every $i$, then $S_1^2=S_0^2=:S^2$, $S_\tau^2=0$ and $V(\widehat{\tau})=S^2\left(\frac{1}{N_1}+\frac{1}{N_0}\right)=\frac{N\,S^2}{N_1N_0}$; moreover $E[SSR]=(N-2)S^2$, so that $E[\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})]=V(\widehat{\tau})$. (L9) [Difference of the two Wald variance forms] $\left(\frac{S_1^2}{N_0}+\frac{S_0^2}{N_1}\right)-\left(\frac{S_1^2}{N_1}+\frac{S_0^2}{N_0}\right)=(S_1^2-S_0^2)\left(\frac{1}{N_0}-\frac{1}{N_1}\right)$, which is zero if and only if $S_1^2=S_0^2$ or $N_1=N_0$; and, for every $z\in\Omega_N$, $\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})-\widehat{V}(\text{Neyman})=\frac{N-1}{N-2}\left(\frac{1}{N_0}-\frac{1}{N_1}\right)(s_1^2-s_0^2)$. (L10) [The witness of (c), for each fixed $m\ge1$] with $N=10m$, $N_1=2m$, $N_0=8m$, $Y_i(0)\in\{1,-1\}$ with $5m$ units at each value and $Y_i(1)=2Y_i(0)$: $\tau=0$, $S_0^2=S_\tau^2=\frac{N}{N-1}$, $S_1^2=\frac{4N}{N-1}$, $V(\widehat{\tau})=\frac{S_1^2}{N_1}+\frac{S_0^2}{N_0}-\frac{S_\tau^2}{N}=\frac{81}{4(N-1)}>\frac{10}{N-1}=\frac{S_1^2}{N_0}+\frac{S_0^2}{N_1}$; for $m=1$: $V(\widehat{\tau})=\frac94$, against $\frac{10}{9}$ and $\frac{85}{36}$. Provenance. None of these is printed in the comment. (L5), the first sentence of (L7) and the first identity of (L9) are the fresh readers' (candidates.json, held_up: ‘the exact randomization variance $S_1^2/N_1+S_0^2/N_0-S_\tau^2/N$ verified by enumeration’). (L10) is the Sol reader's construction (fresh-sol/notes.md, item 6: $N=10$, $n_1=2$, $Y_0=\pm1$, $Y_1=2Y_0$, exact variance $9/4$; limits $81/4$, $10$, $85/4$); the Opus reader's example has $p=1/10$ and the same variances ($361/9>130/9$). (L6), the expectation in (L7) and the second identity of (L9) are not in the readers' records and were checked by complete enumeration in exact arithmetic when this list was fixed. How the limits follow: (a) from (L5); (b) from (L7), and from (L9) with the consistency of $s_1^2$ and $s_0^2$; (c) from (L10).
canonical_claim.note: No finding touches this target; both fresh readers found that every statement in it holds. The Sol reader also computed, for the witness, a limiting rejection probability of about 0.168 for the pooled Wald test at nominal level 0.05; that number rests on the normal approximation and is not part of the target. Neyman (1990) is not staged, so the attribution was not checked against the original.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Section 3, unnumbered display for $\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})-\widehat{V}(\text{Neyman})$ and the sentence that $S_1\neq S_0$ is a necessary condition for the two probability limits to differ; with the display for $\widehat{V}(\text{Neyman})$ of Section 2
canonical_claim.location: p. 347 (PDF p. 2), Section 3, right column; the display for $\widehat{V}(\text{Neyman})$ is at the top of the left column of p. 347, in a sentence that begins on p. 346 (PDF p. 1)
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: [$\widehat{V}(\text{Neyman})$] p. 347: ‘one of Neyman’s variance estimators’; not otherwise defined. S4: $s_1^2/N_1+s_0^2/N_0$. [$\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})$, $\widehat{V}(\text{Fisher})$] S3 and S4, as in P053-T5. [$S_1$, $S_0$] S4; inside the probability limits they are read as the limits $\sigma_1$, $\sigma_0$ (S5). [$\operatorname{plim}$, $o_p(N^{-1})$, $p$, standing conditions] S2 and S5. [Necessary condition] the condition is necessary and not sufficient: the limits also agree when $p=1/2$; the comment says only ‘necessary’. [‘As noted above’] the statement of p. 347 that $\widehat{V}(\text{Fisher})-\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})=o_p(N^{-1})$ when $\tau_N=o(1)$ (target P053-T6(a)).
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: (L6) [Arm sample variances] $E[s_1^2]=S_1^2$ and $E[s_0^2]=S_0^2$; hence $E[\widehat{V}(\text{Neyman})]=\frac{S_1^2}{N_1}+\frac{S_0^2}{N_0}\ge V(\widehat{\tau})$. (L9) [Difference of the two Wald variance forms] $\left(\frac{S_1^2}{N_0}+\frac{S_0^2}{N_1}\right)-\left(\frac{S_1^2}{N_1}+\frac{S_0^2}{N_0}\right)=(S_1^2-S_0^2)\left(\frac{1}{N_0}-\frac{1}{N_1}\right)$, which is zero if and only if $S_1^2=S_0^2$ or $N_1=N_0$; and, for every $z\in\Omega_N$, $\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})-\widehat{V}(\text{Neyman})=\frac{N-1}{N-2}\left(\frac{1}{N_0}-\frac{1}{N_1}\right)(s_1^2-s_0^2)$. (L3) [The OLS variance estimate is the pooled-variance form] For $z\in\Omega_N$, in the least-squares regression of $Y^{\mathrm{obs}}$ on $(1,z)$ the coefficient on $z$ is $\widehat{\tau}$, the residual sum of squares is $SSR$ and $\sum_i(z_i-\bar{z})^2=N_1N_0/N$, so that $\frac{SSR/(N-2)}{\sum_i(z_i-\bar{z})^2}=\frac{SSR}{N-2}\left(\frac{1}{N_1}+\frac{1}{N_0}\right)=\frac{N\,SSR}{N_1N_0(N-2)}$. (L4) [Exact difference] $\widehat{V}(\text{Fisher})=\frac{N\,SSR}{N_1N_0(N-1)}+\frac{\widehat{\tau}^2}{N-1}$ and $\widehat{V}(\text{Fisher})-\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})=\frac{\widehat{\tau}^2}{N-1}-\frac{N\,SSR}{N_1N_0(N-1)(N-2)}=\frac{\widehat{\tau}^2-\widehat{V}(\text{OLS})}{N-1}$, for every $z\in\Omega_N$. Provenance. None of these is printed in the comment. (L3), (L4) and the first identity of (L9) are the fresh readers' (fresh-opus/notes.md, ‘Section 3’; fresh-sol/notes.md, item 5; candidates.json, held_up: the scaled limit is $(S_1^2-S_0^2)(2p-1)/(p(1-p))$). (L6) is classical and the second identity of (L9) follows from the definitions in S4 by algebra; neither is in the readers' records, and both were checked by complete enumeration in exact arithmetic when this list was fixed. How the limits follow: (a) from the consistency of $s_1^2$ and $s_0^2$; (b) and (c) from the second identity of (L9); (d) from (L4) with $\widehat{\tau}\to0$ in probability.
canonical_claim.note: No finding touches this target; both fresh readers found that the display and the necessary condition hold. Ding's equation (7) is not staged.
